title: Google DeepMind’s new AI model can control a robot’s entire body
slides: Can Google DeepMind's AI give robots full body control?
It learns movement from human motion data alone.
The robot never saw certain objects before testing.
Your warehouse bots could work without manual programming.
Start testing your robot's adaptability on one new task.
thread_text:
1. Can robots learn like humans?

DeepMind's AI was trained only on human motion data — no robot-specific programming.

2. No demo, no prep.

The robot faced objects it had never seen before and still adapted without manual code.

3. Full body, zero scripts.

Warehouse bots could gain whole-body control without engineers writing instructions for every move.

4. One test changes everything.

Start by testing your robot's adaptability on a single new task — you might skip months of programming.

5. Try it on one task today.

Take your robot and give it a task it's not trained for. If it fails, what does that tell you?

instagram.caption:
A robot trained only by watching human videos nailed a task it had never seen before — no manual code, no test run.

Google DeepMind’s new model learns full-body control from human motion data alone. The robot handled objects it had never encountered, adapting on the fly without engineers writing a single new instruction. 🧠

That means your warehouse bots could skip months of custom programming for each new task. 🤖

Take your robot and give it one task it wasn't designed for. If it fails, what does that tell you about your current workflow? 💡
